articles.title: "Espero que dios me permita vivir para ver una Euroliga de 30 equipos"
articles.standfirst: Itoudis, técnico del Hapoel Tel Aviv, sueña con la ampliación del torneo y con que el curso de baloncesto en Europa cierre con los playoffs tras competir en Conferencias
articles.summary: Itoudis, técnico del Hapoel Tel Aviv, sueña con la ampliación del torneo y con que el curso de baloncesto en Europa cierre con los playoffs tras competir en Conferencias
articles.body: Dimitris Itoudis vuelve a poner sobre la mesa uno de sus grandes sueños para el futuro del baloncesto europeo: una Euroliga de 30 equipos. El entrenador griego del Hapoel Tel Aviv, doble campeón de la competición con el CSKA Moscú (2016 y 2019), defendió en una entrevista concedida a Mozzartsport.com la expansión de la máxima competición continental y apostó por un nuevo formato que permita cerrar la temporada europea con los playoffs de la Euroliga. Itoudis considera que el torneo ya avanza en esa dirección y confía en que el crecimiento sea progresivo hasta alcanzar los 30 clubes. "Creo que vamos en la dirección correcta: tendremos 24 equipos, quizás lleguemos a 26 y, tal vez en el futuro, si Dios quiere, a lo que sueño y anhelo: 30 clubes". Una cifra que, para el técnico heleno, supondría llevar la competición a una nueva dimensión. Su idea va incluso más allá del número de participantes. Itoudis imagina una Euroliga dividida en conferencias o grupos durante la fase de competición para desembocar después en unos playoffs que decidan el campeón. "Tener conferencias o grupos en los que competir y, finalmente, alcanzar los playoffs. Para mí, ese sería el culmen del baloncesto. Que el último partido de la temporada sea de la Euroliga y que el curso baloncestístico en Europa termine con los playoffs. ¿Se verá en diez años? Pues espero que Dios me permita estar vivo y coleando para que pueda verlo". El entrenador del Hapoel Tel Aviv también encuentra argumentos deportivos para justificar la ampliación. El posible regreso de los clubes rusos, actualmente excluidos de las competiciones europeas, abriría la puerta a nuevos participantes, pero Itoudis recuerda que hay más candidatos interesados en dar el salto. “¿Por qué? Porque ya somos 20, ¿verdad? Creo y espero que los equipos rusos regresen. La FIBA dio luz verde a jugadores, deportistas individuales y árbitros, así que el siguiente paso serían los equipos y los deportes de equipo". Entre los aspirantes menciona a varios históricos y a proyectos con ambición de crecimiento. "Si los equipos rusos regresan, que es mi deseo, ya tenemos otros candidatos. Están el PAOK, el Aris, la Roma, el Hapoel de Tel Aviv y todos los equipos que quieren formar parte de esto, lo que significa que tendremos más equipos que pueden garantizar la estabilidad financiera”. Itoudis entiende que una Euroliga más grande tendría un efecto positivo en todo el ecosistema del baloncesto europeo: “Esto significa más equipos, más jugadores, más entrenadores, más árbitros… Repito, si esta expansión será aceptada o no es un tema de debate, pero creo que debemos crecer”.

articles.title: USA vs. Italy live score, updates, highlights from Caitlin Clark and more in 2026 FIBA World Cup
articles.summary: The Sporting News is tracking live updates from Team USA's second group stage match against Italy.
articles.body:
The U.S. kicked off its FIBA Women's World Cup campaign with aplomb, vanquishing China, 94-71, behind strong displays from its backcourt standouts.

Next up on the docket for Kara Lawson's squad: a tilt against Italy, a side that the Americans dominated during qualifying.

articles.summary: The United States picked up another victory in the group stage of the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin on Sunday, but it was anything but easy.
articles.body:
The United States picked up another victory in the group stage of the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin on Sunday, but it was anything but easy.

An American team that is accustomed to dominating and entered play with a 31-game winning streak in the World Cup needed a second-half comeback to defeat Italy 55-52. The United States is now 2-0 in Group D play after handling China by 33 points in the opener, but Sunday's game that clinched a spot in the quarterfinals required far more late heroics.

2 a.m. fire alarm disrupts FIBA teams at hotel

USA dominates China in FIBA World Cup opener

Chelsea Young hit the game's biggest shot down the stretch, while Jackie Young played lockdown defense on Italy's final possession and finished as her team's leading scorer.

The United States is going to have the most talent every time it steps on the floor in this tournament with a roster that includes Napheesa Collier, Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, Breanna Stewart, Angel Reese and more.

Anything but convincing victories, especially early in the group stage, is surprising, which made Sunday's game so shocking. The Americans looked like they were going through the motions offensively as they didn't hit a single three-pointer in the first half and shot 32 percent from the field, although they still found themselves ahead by six at intermission.

That is because their suffocating defense overwhelmed the Italians with Reese swatting shots down low and even Bueckers getting in on the block party from the backcourt. Italy turned it over 10 times before halftime, which created a number of open looks for the Red, White and blue to overcome some of the offensive woes.

But those offensive woes went nowhere for extended stretches in the third quarter as Italy took the lead.

The guards started forcing contested jumpers, the bigs struggled to deal with swarming double teams and Cecilia Zandalasini started creating scoring opportunities by driving the lane. The Americans went more than five minutes without hitting a field goal and found themselves in comeback mode shortly before the fourth.

It looked as if the United States finally seized some semblance of control when Bueckers hit the team's only three and its defense helped take the lead back, but Italy didn't fold. Instead, it went run-for-run with the powerhouse and had the lead with fewer than four minutes remaining.

However, crunch time belonged to the Americans with Stewart deflecting a pass for a steal, Gray hitting a massive jumper and Young providing just enough defense to clinch the win.

The United States now turns its attention to its final group stage game on Monday against Czechia.

articles.title: Team USA survives upset scare to Italy in FIBA Women's World Cup after poor shooting performance
articles.summary: Team USA has now won 32 consecutive FIBA World Cup games.
articles.body:
Team USA picked up its second Group D victory of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup on Sunday with a narrow 55-52 win over Italy in a game that turned into an upset scare.

The Americans came into the matchup with plenty of confidence. When the U.S. faced Italy in the World Cup qualifiers in March, it won 93-59. Sunday's rematch was a different story.

On the final possession, Italy's Cecilia Zandalasini tried to hit a 3 or draw a foul to tied it, but during the possession, she felt she had been poked in the eye. It wasn't called; she missed a heave, and the clock ran out after USA's Breanna Stewart was able to secure the rebound.

After the final whistle, Zandalasini was incensed and had to be held back by teammates and coaches as she was giving the referees a piece of her mind.

Zandalasini apologized to the referees after the game.

"I would like to apologize for how I reacted in the end. To the opposing team, it was a lot of emotions today, but I should have kept them inside of me a little better. I want to apologize to the referees. It's just when I wear this jersey, it's just a different beast that comes out of me, and now I feel embarrassed for how I reacted."

"I would like to apologize for how I reacted in the end. To the opposing team, it was a lot of emotions today, but I should have kept them inside of me a little better.

I want to apologize to the referees. It's just when I wear this jersey, it's just a different beast that comes out of me, and now I feel embarrassed for how I reacted."

The United States got out to a 19-8 lead in the first quarter using quick possessions and stifling defense. Italy slowly clawed back into the game in the second and third quarters as it played better defense as a team, swapping between zone and man-to-man schemes.

Team USA also went ice cold shooting from the field. The Americans continued to attempt 3s, but didn't make one until Paige Bueckers connected from deep with 1:50 left in the third quarter. Before that first make, the U.S. was 0-for-10 from beyond the arc.

The Americans went into the fourth quarter up 42-39. This started plenty of back-and-forth action in the final frame.

Chelsea Gray hit a jumper with 1:07 left in the game to put the United States up 55-50. Italy responded with a jumper of its own. Jackie Young came down with a huge rebound, but even though the Americans couldn't capitalize on the extra possession, the extra time helped to chip away at the game clock.

The win qualifies Team USA for the quarterfinals of the World Cup. The United States will be back in action Monday against Czechia (2:45 p.m. ET, TNT).

Team USA's offensive pace is not sustainable

Bueckers helped to run a fast-paced offense in the first quarter. The Americans did a good job cleaning up the glass and capitalizing on turnovers.

Team Italy looked slower on offense, trying to be more methodical in attacking Team USA's stout defense. This difference favored the Americans in the first quarter, but Italy in the second quarter.

The Americans were able to rely on their quick possessions, but then, when the shots stopped falling, the Italians took advantage. Team USA shot only 32% in the first half, and the lead was bolstered by 12 free-throw makes compared to Italy's 5.

Their cold spell from the floor continued into the second half. Team USA finished the game 16 of 56 from the floor for a 29% shooting percentage. If the Americans didn't convert 22 of their 30 free-throw attempts, compared to 14 of 20 from the charity stripe for the Italians, Team USA may have lost.

This was Team USA's lowest point total in the FIBA Women's World Cup since 1971.

Can Team USA solve its beyond-the-arc issues?

The Americans ultimately held off Italy, but it wasn't because of an influx of 3s. Team USA went 0-for-3 in both the first and second quarters from beyond the arc.

Team USA finally hit a 3 with 1:50 left in the third quarter. Bueckers tied the game up at 39, but the Americans were 0-for-10 from deep before she hit that shot.

The United States missed another 3-pointer and finished the game a measly 1-of-12 from 3-point range.

Caitlin Clark, Kahleah Copper, and Rhyne Howard went a combined 0-for-7 from beyond the arc.

The U.S. played clean basketball in its first game against China, committing only eight turnovers. Against Italy, the United States committed 13 turnovers.

The good news for the Americans is that the Italians had 16 turnovers, so that metric did favor Team USA, but it is an easy aspect of the game to improve upon before the next matchup.

Team USA continues to have a balanced attack

If you watch these WNBA stars play for their respective teams, it is not uncommon for them to lead their team in points by a wide margin.

The Americans' All-Star team has done a great job in two games of spreading the ball around. Against China, Team USA was led by Bueckers, Clark, and Howard, who each had 14 points.

Against Italy, only Jackie Young finished with 10 points. Angel Reese had eight points off the bench, and Napheesa Collier, Copper, and Aliyah Boston each finished with six points apiece.

articles.standfirst: EE.UU. gana sin brillantez ni acierto (52-55) a un rival que la hizo sufrir hasta el final y estuvo a punto de romper su récord de imbatibilidad de los últimos 20 años (69-0)
articles.summary: Gana sin brillantez (XX-XX) a una Italia que plantó cara en la primera parte
articles.body: Estados Unidos estuvo a punto de perder su primer partido en los últimos 20 años. Desde que cayese en las semifinales del Mundial 2006 ante Rusia (75-68) no conocía la derrota, acumulando un balance sideral entre Juegos y Mundiales de 69-0. Pero el 'Dream Team' estadounidense estuvo a punto de ver rota esa estratosférica racha ante la sorprendente Italia, que finalmente cedió pero la llevó al límite (52-55). Las transalpinas, comandadas por Villa (6+5), Santucci (9) y Zandalasini (14+7) tuvieron contra las cuerdas al ogro estadounidense, que perpetró uno de los partidos más terrenales que se le recuerda desde la final de los Juegos de París que ganaron ante Francia (67-66). De hecho, sólo fue capaz de anotar 16 canastas en juego en todo el partido (16/56), con 15/44 t2 y 1/12 triples, además de sumar 14 pérdidas. Ese atasco pocas veces visto en una selección tan superior fue aprovechado por una Italia que se creció viendo que el Goliat del basket femenino titubeaba y nunca le perdió la cara al partido. Llegó a tener tres puntos de ventaja en el tercer cuarto tras un parcial de 15-6 liderado por Zandalasini (39-36, min 28). Pero Bueckers comandó un 0-6 con el único triple en el partido de su equipo, que tomó aire (39-42). El último acto fue un cara y cruz, con Santucci manteniendo la delantera de Italia (50-48, min 36). Y ahí se les acabaron la gasolina, el acierto y la fe a las transalpinas, que encajaron un parcial de 2-7 perdiendo una oportunidad única en sus vidas. Zandalasini tuvo un último triple para mandar el partido a la prórroga, pero falló reclamando una falta de Young que los árbitros no apreciaron. La propia Young (10+4+3) fue la única estadounidense que llegó a la decena en anotación. Estuvo secundada por Stewart (5+11), Reese (8+3) y Cooper (6+4) las únicas que se salvaron de un día negro de su equipo del que no se libró ni la mediática Caitlin Clark, que acabó con un punto (0/3 t2, 0/3 t3 y 1/2 tl), cuatro rebotes y una asistencia. Las estrellas estadounidenses no brillaron y sus rivales directos, Francia, Australia y ojalá que España, ya han visto que el 'Dream Team' es vulnerable.

articles.title: Shaq’s Recent Take On Inside The NBA Is Hitting Me Hard After Charles Barkley’s Retirement News
articles.summary: This is tough.
articles.body:

This past week, Inside the NBA fans received some surprising and disappointing news. Longtime series co-host Charles Barkley announced that the upcoming season would be his last on the show and, if that wasn't sad enough, he also revealed that Ernie Johnson planned to leave as well. Johnson and Barkley's departures will mark the end of a major era when it comes to sports-centric television. And what has me even deeper in my feelings about this is that the news comes on the heels of some sweet comments made by Shaq.

For nearly 15 years now, Johnson and Barkley have shared a table with Kenny Smith and Shaquille O'Neal, at which they've discussed the biggest developments in the NBA. The show may not include much analysis , but it does offer up some solid insights and hilarious moments from Shaq and Barkley . The "Diesel" recently discussed the show, specifically its historic move from TNT to ESPN . While sharing his feeling, the multihyphenate weighed in on why the show gels and how he's feeling going into the upcoming season:

Whenever you take a program people have watched for years and put it in a new environment, there's going to be an adjustment period. People are always going to compare everything; it just comes with the territory. For us, the job hasn't changed. Ernie, Kenny, Chuck and I are there to talk basketball, be honest, have fun and deliver the chemistry our viewers enjoy because that's when the show works best.

I couldn't agree more with the comments that the four-time NBA champion shared with ClutchPoints , especially the point about the collaboration between the four hosts. Earlier this year, O'Neal shared more thoughts on what makes Inside successful and, at that point, he broke down the varied attributes that each host brings to the proceedings. Considering these thoughts, it's bittersweet to think that just weeks later, it looks like the band is set to be broken up, per the sentiments shared by Barkley.

Charles Barkley Got Real About His Intention To Retire

The former Phoenix Sun shared his retirement comments during a recent appearance on The Bill Simmons Podcast . Ironically, Barkley began speaking on the topic after Simmons joked that ahead of this season, Barkley hadn't made any retirement declarations. The Inside alum then laid out the various times he's told his employers of his desire to step away from the job. Barkley eventually said that Johnson asked him to stay on two additional years before last season in order to save jobs. The Emmy winner continued:

I said, 'Ernie, I'll stay for two more years.' But he says, 'Chuck, I'm planning on retiring in two years.' So me and Ernie are a package deal. So, to answer your question, Ernie said to me, 'Chuck, would you please stay for two more years?' I said, 'You know what, Ernie? I love you, man. You're the best.' I said, 'I'll stay for two more years.' So, right now, unless Ernie changes his mind, next year is my last year, 100%.

Fans may be aware that this isn't the first time the "Round Mound of Rebound" has spoken about walking away from his broadcasting career. It was in the summer of 2024 that Barkley announced he was retiring after the 2024-2025 NBA season. That announcement came in the midst of the Inside cancellation situation , which stemmed from TNT's parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery, losing the broadcast rights to the league. Before the ESPN deal was announced, though, Barkley confirmed he'd remain with TNT Sports to see his ten-year contract through.

Charles Barkley seems to be standing firm in his retirement position this time around and, as tough as it is to fathom, I do understand his feelings. Even over the past several years, Barkley's been adamant about not feeling the need to be on TV all the time. Still, the former athlete has affection for his colleagues, as he also said during the interview that he had "love" for the people he'd worked with for "26, 27 years."

If Barkley and Ernie Johnson do end up signing off for the final time at the end of this coming season, I'll remain grateful for their contributions to sports and TV. More immediately, though, I look forward to seeing the winning dynamic described by Shaq for one more year. Check out Inside the NBA when it returns to ESPN this fall amid the 2026 TV schedule .
